solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Whisky one's missing? Nearly all love wine and soda

indicators.note: one is the Roman numeral I, so 'one's missing' says an I drops out of the spirit

parts.note: whisky is a spirit

indicators.note: nearly all of the word for love keeps everything but its final letter

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, i.e. zero

explanation.surface: A drinker finds the whisky gone and settles, nearly happily, for a long drink of wine and soda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's missing' takes an I out of SPIRIT to leave SPRIT; 'Nearly all' trims ZERO to ZER.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritzer is a long drink made by topping up white wine with soda water.

clue.text: Dropping off pair with hands bleeding

parts.note: South and North form a partnership in bridge, a pair holding hands of cards
a wound that bleeds is oozing

explanation.surface: A couple holding hands while both are bleeding.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South are partners, each holding a hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping off means falling asleep, i.e. taking a nap.

clue.text: Concrete mass in field

parts.note: concrete means real, actual
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A mass of concrete poured in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain or sphere of activity, as in 'the realm of science'.

clue.text: Music played at Ritz — and Oz jail

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A band performs at the Ritz hotel and in an Australian prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of jazz in the early New Orleans manner, also called trad.

clue.text: Very black time I had in middle of Greece's recession

indicators.note: in places the other letters inside the central pair from the country's name
middle of takes the central letters of the country's name

parts.note: BB marks a very soft, black pencil
I'd is a contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Greece's economy sinks into a dark time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes EE from GREECE; BB is the soft-pencil grade.
explanation.definitionFit: An ebb tide is the falling tide as the sea recedes.

clue.text: Whistling device

definitions.meaning: the whistling sound of laboured breathing
a clever scheme or trick, a sense of the word in British slang

explanation.surface: A gadget that whistles, like a kettle or a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a whistling breath and, in British slang, a clever ploy or scheme.

clue.text: Dance tantalizes with nothing exotic

indicators.note: exotic suggests the letters taken into strange new arrangement

parts.note: O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: An exotic dancer teases while wearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hesitation waltz is a waltz with pauses held on a step.

clue.text: Short letter recalled gym has been made available for hire

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the gym letters are read the other way

parts.note: PE is physical education, gym

parts.words: has been made available for hire
parts.note: a property put up for hire is to let

explanation.surface: A short note says the recalled gym is now for rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been made available for hire' is read as IS TO LET.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistolet is a little epistle, a brief letter.

clue.text: Frenzy merely shows one used to get a reaction

definitions.text: one used to get a reaction

indicators.note: shows means the run of letters is on view inside the two words

explanation.surface: A wild outburst merely shows someone trying to provoke a response.
explanation.definitionFit: Enzymes are biological catalysts used to drive chemical reactions.

clue.text: One grabbed twice by bisexual tart

indicators.note: twice says the one is taken in a second time, at a second spot
grabbed by the slang word puts the one inside it

parts.note: AC/DC is slang for bisexual
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bisexual tart grabs one person twice.
explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC takes in an I twice: AC-I-D-I-C.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp to the taste, like a tart fruit; a synonym.

clue.text: Sailor also called for port

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman
aka abbreviates 'also known as'

explanation.surface: A sailor, also known as a port name, gets called up for shore duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major Japanese seaport on Osaka Bay.

clue.text: County girl with unknown double cocktail

parts.note: Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire, an English county near London
Fi is a short form of the girl's name Fiona

indicators.note: double asks for the unknown letter to be written twice

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A country girl and a mystery companion order a double cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is Buckinghamshire, a county west of London; algebra's unknowns are x, y and z.
explanation.definitionFit: Buck's fizz is a mixed drink of champagne and orange juice.

clue.text: Senseless bringing doctor in if I doze off

indicators.note: bringing one thing in puts it inside the other
in places the doctor's letters within the scrambled ones
off means gone wrong, so the letters of 'if I doze' are rearranged

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Someone warns they will be left senseless if they nod off, so a doctor is called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the letters of 'if I doze'; 'bringing ... in' sets the doctor inside them. MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a standard crossword doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To be turned into a zombie is to be left dazed and without feeling or awareness.

clue.text: It might be something polar bear misses at first

parts.note: to bear something is to carry or tote it

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of misses

explanation.surface: A polar bear on the hunt keeps missing its first lunge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polar' is not about bears: a totem pole is a carved pole, so the image is something that comes as a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved emblem of this kind is often set up as a tall pole, hence a 'pole' thing.

clue.text: As female maybe avoiding relations that are unpopular, outspoken

indicators.note: outspoken means spoken out loud, so the sound of the phrase gives the entry

parts.note: things that are unpopular are things which none like

explanation.surface: A woman shuns unpopular relatives and is frank about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' are sexual relations, not relatives; a female shunning them lives like a convent sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving like a member of a religious order of women, sworn to chastity.

clue.text: Figured men should support miners

indicators.note: in a down clue, to support something is to sit beneath it, so the men go below the miners

parts.note: the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, Britain's miners' union
the men are two named fellows, Eric and Al

explanation.surface: Men are expected to stand behind the miners in their dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' gives two names, ERIC and AL; 'support' in a down clue puts them below the miners' union, NUM, a British trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Figured can mean expressed in figures, i.e. in number form.

clue.text: Lowers cape, heading off to fight

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the word for fight

parts.note: a battle is a fight

explanation.surface: A bullfighter lowers the cape as he heads off to the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowers' reads as a verb but means things that low, i.e. moo.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows low, so cows and their kind are, punningly, lowers.

clue.text: Slothful water carrier who fell lifting tool

parts.note: slothful means lazy
Jack fell down while fetching a pail of water in the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: The idle lad who tumbled carrying water ends up lifting a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, Jack and Jill fetch water and Jack falls down the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy jack is a compound jack with a lever, used for raising loads.

clue.text: We agree with that policeman's reforms

parts.note: amen is said by a congregation to show agreement
DS is a detective sergeant, with the 's giving S

explanation.surface: A crowd backs the policeman's changes to the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'policeman's' gives DS: D for detective, S for sergeant.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends is to put right, so as a verb it means improves or corrects.

clue.text: Sons each bearing something refreshing

parts.note: S abbreviates son
a bearing is an air, a manner

explanation.surface: Boys each bring along a refreshing drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The fresh air by the coast is famed for being invigorating.

clue.text: State regularly backed Maoist law on rich

indicators.note: backed means the picked letters are read in reverse order
regularly takes every other letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: A country sets a Maoist law against the wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters A I T A O R C, and 'backed' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a sovereign country in south-east Europe.

clue.text: King's maybe a merry one, crossing stage

indicators.note: crossing means the merry king's name spans round the stage

parts.note: Old King Cole was a merry old soul in the nursery rhyme
a leg is a stage of a journey

explanation.surface: A king, merry as ever, stepping over a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: King's College is a college at Cambridge and in London, an example of one.

clue.text: Lines of volunteers land faraway in it

indicators.note: in places the volunteers and the land within the word for it

parts.note: it, meaning sex appeal, is SA
the TA is the Territorial Army, British volunteer soldiers
NZ is New Zealand, a land far away

explanation.surface: Verses about volunteers landing in some far country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' as sex appeal gives SA; the TA was Britain's volunteer reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem.

clue.text: Highland track crossed by crowd going the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way says the whole assembly is read backwards
crossed by means the crowd's letters go across, around the track

parts.note: a lot is a crowd or group
RY abbreviates railway, a track

explanation.surface: A mountain trail blocked by a crowd heading the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossed by' puts the track inside the crowd, and 'going the wrong way' reverses the lot. RY is the usual crossword abbreviation for railway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine region of Austria and Italy, mountainous country.

clue.text: See that wallaby jumps across with appropriate bounds?

indicators.note: across means the scrambled letters stretch round the other letters
jumps suggests the wallaby's letters leaping about into a new order

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold

explanation.surface: Look how the wallaby leaps about within proper limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wallaby' looks like part of the scene but is the anagram fodder; 'jumps' rearranges it and 'across' wraps it round LO, an old word for 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a permitted way, i.e. within the limits that are proper, with a pun on the wallaby's bounds.

clue.text: Spot on head of Indian

parts.note: a spot is a bind, a tight situation

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of Indian

explanation.surface: A decorative spot worn on the forehead of an Indian woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a spot' and 'in a bind' both mean in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A bindi is the coloured dot worn on the forehead in South Asian tradition.

clue.text: Caught in trap, live, outside in fruit tree

indicators.note: in puts the cricket letter for caught inside the trap

parts.note: a net is a trap
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: outside means the word for live goes round the second in

parts.note: to live is to be, as in 'we are'

explanation.surface: Something trapped and living, snug in a fruit tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned peach, and the tree bearing it.

clue.text: Girl's new top: ace for going about!

indicators.note: going about means the top and the ace surround the abbreviation for new

parts.note: a lid is a top
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A girl shows off her new top, swapping an ace for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a woman's given name.

clue.text: In a jacket that's too short

definitions.note: a fire that is in is still burning

indicators.note: too short means the jacket loses its final letter

parts.note: a blazer is a jacket

explanation.surface: Someone squeezed into a jacket that doesn't fit, its sleeves riding up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the definition: a fire that is 'in' is alight.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire still in is burning, so in the crossword sense the word means on fire.

clue.text: US film producer does prison flogging — audio version

indicators.note: an audio version is one heard, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: nick is British slang for prison, and flogging means selling, so 'flogging prison' is sells nick

explanation.surface: A Hollywood mogul is caught selling off a jail, in a recorded account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogging' is British slang for selling, not whipping; 'nick' is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: David O. Selznick produced Gone with the Wind and other Hollywood classics.
